reasons: Cached opinion header confirms '390 U.S. 377 (1968)', caption 'SIMMONS ET AL. v. UNITED STATES', 'Decided March 18, 1968' — matches citation, title, year.

Holding-1 verbatim in opinion Part I: 'convictions based on eyewitness identification at trial following a pretrial identification by photograph will be set aside on that ground only if the photographic identification procedure was so impermissibly suggestive as to give rise to a very substantial likelihood of irreparable misidentification.'

Holding-2 verbatim in opinion Part III: 'we therefore hold that when a defendant testifies in support of a motion to suppress evidence on Fourth Amendment grounds, his testimony may not thereafter be admitted against him at trial on the issue of guilt unless he makes no objection.'

Part I of the opinion establishes the photographic-identification due-process standard, squarely a progeny of Stovall v. Denno in the eyewitness-identification line — doctrinal fit for 'Key — Progeny' on Eyewitness Identification.
